hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: We must pick nums[0] and then k - 1 additional starting indices from 1 to n - 1.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: All chosen starting indices must fall within a sliding window of size at most dist.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Slide a window of size dist + 1 across nums[1:] while tracking the sum of the smallest k - 1 elements.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def minimumCost(self, nums: list[int], k: int, dist: int) -> int:
        k -= 1
        window = sorted(nums[1:dist + 2])
        cur_sum = sum(window[:k])
        ans = cur_sum
        for i in range(dist + 2, len(nums)):
            out_val = nums[i - dist - 1]
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(window, out_val)
            window.pop(idx)
            in_val = nums[i]
            bisect.insort(window, in_val)
            cur_sum = sum(window[:k])
            ans = min(ans, cur_sum)
        return nums[0] + ans
```

complexity.notes: Sliding window with sorted array insertion or two heaps.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Re-evaluating the top k elements naively takes O(n * dist log dist) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(dist) space for sorted window buffer.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulate as sliding window minimum top-k sum problem.
